content: Before taking isoniazid, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid alcohol while taking isoniazid, as it can increase the risk of liver disease. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, be aware that it may contain sugar. Exercise caution if you have diabetes or any condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. During pregnancy, isoniazid should only be used if clearly necessary. While this medication passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, consult your doctor for guidance. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses on isoniazid and experiences severe symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests, such as sputum tests, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts, should be performed. Ensure you attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose of isoniazid, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. If you are on a weekly dosing schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you remember the missed dose the next day or later, consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. Store isoniazid at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Take isoniazid on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. If you are using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with a special measuring device or spoon. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. If you are taking it daily, take it at the same time each day. If you are on a weekly schedule, take it on the same day(s) of the week and at the same time. Continue taking isoniazid and any other prescribed TB medications for the full duration of the treatment, even if symptoms disappear. Your doctor may also recommend taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) to prevent certain side effects, such as nerve problems, associated with isoniazid. Isoniazid may interact with foods containing tyramine or histamine, such as cheese, red wine, and certain types of fish. This interaction can cause increased blood pressure, skin flushing, headache, dizziness, or a rapid/pounding heartbeat. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Your doctor may advise you to follow a special diet while taking this medication. Common side effects of isoniazid include nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about isoniazid. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
